title: A bigger star's clock
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Massive stars have more fuel but consume it at a much higher rate. Their lives are generally much shorter than those of low-mass stars.

misconception: A learner may choose: It is always longer because it starts with more fuel
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: How does a very massive star's lifetime generally compare with that of a low-mass star?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: How does a very massive star's lifetime generally compare with that of a low-mass star? It is shorter because it uses fuel much faster. Massive stars have more fuel but consume it at a much higher rate. Their lives are generally much shorter than those of low-mass stars.
Visual caption: Massive stars burn faster. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: How does a very massive star's lifetime generally compare with that of a low-mass star?
options: It is shorter because it uses fuel much faster
It is always longer because it starts with more fuel
Every star has exactly the same lifetime
recall.why: Massive stars have more fuel but consume it at a much higher rate. Their lives are generally much shorter than those of low-mass stars.
